cases.purpose: script record relays typed input to the recorded child, puts the outer terminal in raw/no-echo mode while recording and restores it, gives the inner pty the initial 24x80 size, and propagates a 30x100 resize to the inner pty while recording it as an advanced-timing SIGWINCH event and an asciinema 'r' event
cases.oracle: contract: loadables/script.c record (help: 'Spawn CMD on a pty; record streams'; -m advanced timing 'S <delay> SIGWINCH ROWS= COLS=' and 'H' headers; asciinema v2 header and [t, "r", "COLSxROWS"] events) and util-linux script(1) advanced-timing format
cases.comparison: semantic: inner 'stty size' output seen on the outer terminal before and after the resize; exact input log; timing/cast lines matched by format-anchored patterns in-script (times vary); termios checked during recording and fully restored after
cases.script:
script record -m advanced -c '/usr/bin/stty size; read -r l; printf "<%s>\n" "$l"; /usr/bin/stty size' -O out -I in -T tim -A cast
printf '%s\n' "$?" > status
g=/usr/bin/grep
{
$g -qx 'H 0.000000 COLUMNS 80' tim && echo tim-cols-80
$g -qx 'H 0.000000 LINES 24' tim && echo tim-lines-24
$g -Eq '^S [0-9]+\.[0-9]{6} SIGWINCH ROWS=30 COLS=100$' tim && echo tim-sigwinch-30x100
$g -Eq '^I [0-9]+\.[0-9]{6} [1-9][0-9]*$' tim && echo tim-input-event
IFS= read -r head < cast
[[ $head =~ ^\{\"version\":2,\"width\":80,\"height\":24,\"timestamp\":[0-9]+\}$ ]] && echo cast-header-80x24
$g -Eq '^\[[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}, "r", "100x30"\]$' cast && echo cast-resize-100x30
o=$(<out)
[[ $o == *'24 80'*'<hi>'*'30 100'* ]] && echo out-sizes-and-line
} > checks
rm -f tim cast out

expected_files.checks:
tim-cols-80
tim-lines-24
tim-sigwinch-30x100
tim-input-event
cast-header-80x24
cast-resize-100x30
out-sizes-and-line
